core.text: Attack the preferred dependency that refresh immediately before every commit is necessary for reliable correction. Retain the stipulated row-bound editor and initially loaded S0; omit all intermediate refreshes. Do not replace row binding, hide refreshes inside inspection, or restore the dependency through a mismatch correction loop.

Transfer the account targeted for failure: reliable, latest-compliant correction requires per-commit refresh. Its necessity remains unproved. O5 establishes one selection-then-refresh wrong-target write, not that freshness prevents errors. A successful replay without intermediate refresh would falsify necessity within this model; that replay and account failure have not been observed.

Preserve the valued outcome unchanged: exactly K2, K5 and K7 checked, the other five unchecked, zero incorrect-key writes including repaired ones, unchanged read-only scores, latest snapshot loaded before submission, and completion within ten simulated minutes. Key-persistent local statuses make this a proposed surviving outcome, not an executed success.

Fresh builder: start all-unchecked S0. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1, commit during 1-2; inspect/select K5 during 2-3, commit during 3-4; inspect/select K7 during 4-5, commit during 5-6; refresh during 6-7 to load S2. With S0 retained, selected rows remain 2, 5 and 7 respectively until commit. Predict writes K2, K5 and K7 only; the final refresh should reorder display while preserving statuses by key.

Record action times, refresh count, loaded snapshots, selected rows, intended keys and every actual written key/value. Accept the hypothesized counterexample only if logged writes match all three intended keys, final statuses exactly match the target map and loaded S2 satisfies final freshness. Any wrong-key write disqualifies success even if subsequently repaired.

residue.text: K5 and K7 both score 75 in S2; score-only identification is ambiguous. Verify immutable keys and statuses explicitly. The tie does not require fresh scores before each commit.
Mismatch-triggered refresh causing recurrent miswrites is an unobserved return-path hypothesis. Transfer no claim of repeated feedback from the one stipulated miswrite.

This candidate concerns eight invented records only. Real binding, detection and interruption costs remain unknown; concurrency, deletion and load failure are outside the model. Production tools and human participants are unavailable.

tension.account_a: Per-commit freshness is necessary for reliable correction, so retaining S0 across all commits prevents the valued outcome.
tension.account_b: Stable selected-row identity suffices for fixed-key correction; final freshness alone can preserve the valued outcome.
tension.prediction_a: The declared no-intermediate-refresh replay must fail at least one acceptance condition, even after loading S2.
tension.prediction_b: The replay should write only K2, K5 and K7, preserve the exact status map and load S2 in seven action minutes. Verified success would reject account_a within the synthetic model.
